instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight, drain, and parboil in fresh water for 5–7 minutes. Drain.
instructions.2: Make kibbeh paste as for the fried kubeiba discs in this collection (bulgur soaked for an hour, then minced repeatedly with beef, fat and onion into a soft dough).
instructions.3: Either shape it into hollow balls filled with spiced minced beef and pine nuts, or cut it into thin discs. Do not fry them.
instructions.4: Put the kibbeh in a pot with the chickpeas.
instructions.5: Stir the egg white into the yogurt to stop it curdling and press it through a sieve over the kibbeh.
instructions.6: Cook uncovered for 60–90 minutes.
instructions.7: Sprinkle with the mint and serve hot or cold.

ec-105.title: Cauliflower Stewed with Beef and Tomato (‘Arnabit Matbukh)
ec-105.culturalNotes: Recipe 105, page 49 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Break the cauliflower into florets and cut the meat into bite-sized pieces. Peel and dice the tomatoes and chop the onions very finely.
instructions.2: Fry the onions in the oil until pale yellow, add the tomatoes and cook for 7–10 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the meat with salt and pepper and cook for about 20 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the cauliflower and simmer for about 10 minutes, until tender.
instructions.5: With garlic instead of tomato (recipe 106 in the book): fry the onions, brown the meat until it reabsorbs its juices, cover with water, add 7–10 halved garlic cloves with the seasoning and cook for 20 minutes, then add the cauliflower for 10 minutes.

ec-109.title: Baked Chicken with Tomatoes and Onions (Tagin Firakh)
ec-109.culturalNotes: Recipe 109, page 50 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut each chicken into 4–6 pieces.
instructions.2: Mix the spice with salt and pepper and rub it lightly over the chicken.
instructions.3: Lay the pieces in a lightly greased roasting pan and cover them with the seasoned onions and tomatoes.
instructions.4: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 60–90 minutes, basting with the pan juices.
instructions.5: Thicken the juices with cornflour if you like.
instructions.6: With carrots and celery (recipe 110 in the book): brown chopped onions and celery in oil, cover the chicken with them and with parboiled carrot rounds and halved garlic cloves, pour meat stock over and bake the same way.

ec-115.title: Chicken in Mastic Milk Sauce (Firakh Matbukha bi-l-Laban)
ec-115.culturalNotes: Recipe 115, page 53 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut each chicken into 6–8 pieces.
instructions.2: Heat the oil, stir in the mastic for 10 seconds, add the chicken, cover at once and turn off the heat. Leave for 1–2 minutes so the chicken takes on the scent.
instructions.3: Turn the heat back on and brown the chicken, then lift it out.
instructions.4: Fry the flour in the same oil until light brown. Off the heat, whisk in the milk a little at a time until smooth.
instructions.5: Return to the heat, season, and when it bubbles add the chicken.
instructions.6: Cook uncovered for about 20 minutes, until tender.

ec-116.title: Chicken with Green Olives (Firakh bi-l-Zatun al-Akhdar)
ec-116.culturalNotes: Recipe 116, page 53 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut each chicken into 4–6 pieces. Boil the olives in fresh water for 1 minute, drain, pit and halve them.
instructions.2: Heat the oil, stir in the mastic for 10 seconds, add the chicken, cover tightly and turn off the heat for 1–2 minutes, then fry the chicken until browned and lift it out.
instructions.3: Soften the onion in the same oil and set it aside with the chicken.
instructions.4: Fry the flour until golden. Off the heat, whisk in 1 cup of warm water a little at a time.
instructions.5: Return to the heat and, when the gravy bubbles, add the chicken, onion, salt and pepper. Cook over a very low heat for about 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the olives and lemon juice and simmer for 2–3 minutes more.

ec-117.title: Giblet-Stuffed Chicken, Boiled then Fried (Firakh Mahshiya wi Mihammara)
ec-117.culturalNotes: Recipe 117, page 54 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-117-i1.name: Chickens, About 1 Kg Each, With Giblets

ec-117-i2.name: Onions (2 For The Stuffing, 1 For The Broth)

instructions.1: Finely chop two onions and cut the gizzards and hearts into very small pieces. Mix them with the spice, salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Stuff the chickens with the mixture and sew them up.
instructions.3: Bring enough water to half-cover the chickens to the boil with the remaining onion and salt, add the chickens and cook for about 20 minutes, then lift them out.
instructions.4: Heat oil in another pot, stir in the mastic for 10 seconds, add the chickens, cover tightly and turn off the heat for 1–2 minutes.
instructions.5: Fry the chickens, turning them until browned all over.

ec-118.title: Giblet-Stuffed Roast Chicken (Firakh Mahshiya wi Mashwiya)
ec-118.culturalNotes: Recipe 118, page 54 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-118-i1.name: Chickens, About 1 Kg Each, With Giblets

instructions.1: Chop the onions very finely and cut the gizzards and hearts into very small pieces. Season, add the spice and mix.
instructions.2: Stuff the chickens and sew them up.
instructions.3: Mix the tomato paste, lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper and rub it all over the chickens.
instructions.4: Roast in a hot oven, basting two or three times with the juices.

ec-120.title: Lebanese Lemon Chicken with Olives (Djaj bi Leimoon Hamed)
ec-120.culturalNotes: Recipe 120, page 56 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the chickens into neat joints and fry them lightly in oil; set aside.
instructions.2: Put the onions, garlic, coriander and parsley in a pot, add the saffron and leave over a very low heat until soft.
instructions.3: Add the chicken with its oil, salt, pepper and 1 cup of hot water. Cover and cook slowly, stirring now and then.
instructions.4: When the chicken is done, move it to a platter. Mash the vegetables well, add the lemon juice and olives and let it bubble for 2–3 minutes.
instructions.5: Pour the sauce over the chicken and serve.

ec-121.title: Chicken in Pomegranate and Walnut Sauce (Fesenjan)
ec-121.culturalNotes: Recipe 121, page 56 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the chickens into neat joints, fry them lightly on all sides and keep them warm.
instructions.2: Soften the onions in the same oil.
instructions.3: Add the walnuts, broth, sugar, pomegranate juice, salt and pepper and cook until the sauce thickens.
instructions.4: Return the chicken and cook over a low heat for 20–25 minutes more.

ec-122.title: Lebanese Rice-Stuffed Chicken, Boiled then Fried (Djaj Mihshy)
ec-122.culturalNotes: Recipe 122, page 57 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-122-i1.name: Chickens, About 1 Kg Each, With Giblets

instructions.1: Dice the giblets and mix them with the rice, spice, salt and pepper. Stuff the chickens and truss or sew them closed.
instructions.2: Bring 4 cups of water to the boil with the onion and seasoning, add the chickens and cook for 20–30 minutes. Lift them out and keep warm.
instructions.3: Heat oil, stir in the mastic for a few seconds, add the chickens, cover tightly and turn off the heat for 2–3 minutes.
instructions.4: Uncover and fry the chickens until nicely browned.
instructions.5: Cut them into joints, heap the stuffing in the middle of a dish and arrange the chicken around it. Moisten the stuffing with a little warm broth if you like.

ec-123.title: Lebanese Rice-Stuffed Roast Chicken (Djaj Mihshy)
ec-123.culturalNotes: Recipe 123, page 57 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-123-i1.name: Chickens, About 1 Kg Each, With Giblets

instructions.1: Dice the giblets and mix them with the rice, spice, salt and pepper. Stuff the chickens and truss or sew them closed.
instructions.2: Thin the tomato paste with the lemon juice, add salt, pepper and the oil, and rub the mixture over the chickens inside and out.
instructions.3: Roast, basting often with the lemon mixture.

ec-124.title: Chicken Simmered in Yogurt with Mint (Firakh Matbukha bi-l-Zabadi)
ec-124.culturalNotes: Recipe 124, page 58 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the chickens into neat joints and fry them lightly in olive oil.
instructions.2: Stir the egg white into the yogurt to keep it from splitting and press it through a sieve over the chicken.
instructions.3: Season and cook uncovered for about 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Thicken with the cornflour, move to a serving dish and sprinkle with the mint.

ec-125.title: Sumac-Onion Chicken Baked in Bread (Frakh Mashwiya bi-l-Summa’)
ec-125.culturalNotes: Recipe 125, page 58 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Grate the onions and mix with the sumac, salt, pepper and olive oil.
instructions.2: Rub the chickens with the mixture and push the rest inside them.
instructions.3: Wrap each chicken in a loaf of bread, then in foil.
instructions.4: Cook slowly in the middle of a low, preheated oven until the chicken is tender.

ec-135.title: Tunisian Fish Couscous with Fish Balls (Couscous bil Hout)
ec-135.culturalNotes: Recipe 135, page 62 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-135-i4.name: Marinade: Fennel Seeds And Caraway Seeds

ec-135-i7.name: Fish Balls: Grated Onion, 3–5 Crushed Garlic Cloves, 1 Egg And Half A Stale Loaf

ec-135-i8.name: Fish Balls: Chopped Parsley, A Dash Of Harissa And Paprika

ec-135-i10.name: Onions, Zucchini, Carrots, Artichoke Hearts And Tomatoes

ec-135-i11.name: Cloves, A Piece Of Cinnamon Bark And Caraway Seeds

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight, then boil them in fresh water until tender. Drain, keeping the liquid.
instructions.2: Mix the marinade ingredients and leave the fish fillets in it for 1–2 hours.
instructions.3: Fish balls: moisten the bread with water. Steam and flake the whiting and mix it with a purée of the onion and garlic, the paprika, harissa, parsley, beaten egg, bread, salt and pepper. Roll into small balls, fry until brown and keep warm.
instructions.4: Vegetables: brown the grated onions in oil, then stir in the sliced zucchini and carrots, chopped artichokes and diced tomatoes until coated with oil. Add the spices tied in muslin, the chickpeas and enough of their liquid to cover, and cook over a low heat.
instructions.5: Sprinkle the couscous with cold water and steam it in a perforated steamer set over the vegetable pot, covered. Once or twice, uncover, sprinkle with a little cold water and fluff the grains with a fork so they do not form lumps. Keep steaming until the vegetables are tender.
instructions.6: Brush the marinade off the fish and grill the fillets on both sides.
instructions.7: Pile the couscous in a serving bowl, top with the grilled fish and fish balls, and serve the vegetables separately.

ec-136.title: Tunisian Couscous with Mutton and Dates (Couscous bi Tamr)
ec-136.culturalNotes: Recipe 136, page 64 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Peel and dice the carrots and turnips.
instructions.2: Boil the meat and vegetables in salted water.
instructions.3: When the meat is nearly done, sprinkle the couscous with water and steam it over the pot for 5–7 minutes.
instructions.4: Uncover, sprinkle lightly with water and break up any lumps with a fork.
instructions.5: Stone and roughly chop the dates, mix them into the couscous and return it to steam over the meat until both are fully cooked. Keep them separate.
instructions.6: Pour a ladle of the meat broth over the garlic, harissa and chili and boil hard until reduced by half.
instructions.7: Serve the couscous, the meat and the sauce separately.

ec-138.title: Lebanese Chicken Maghrabiyeh
ec-138.culturalNotes: Recipe 138, page 65 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the chicken into neat joints.
instructions.2: Bring water to the boil with the onions, mastic, salt and pepper, add the chicken and cook.
instructions.3: About 10–15 minutes before the chicken is done, sprinkle the couscous with water and steam it over the broth, uncovering once or twice to break up lumps with a fork and sprinkle with more cold water.
instructions.4: When the couscous is tender, move it to a deep bowl and keep warm.
instructions.5: Lift out the chicken and fry the joints in oil.
instructions.6: Mash the onion into the broth, thicken it, check the seasoning and serve it separately as a sauce.

ec-147.title: Fried Eggplant Baked in Tahini (Bitingan Ma’li bi-l-Tahina)
ec-147.culturalNotes: Recipe 147, page 68 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice the eggplants lengthwise about 2 cm thick, sprinkle with salt and leave for at least an hour. Squeeze gently, drain and pat dry.
instructions.2: Deep-fry the slices until dark brown and drain on absorbent paper.
instructions.3: Make a thin tahini sauce: whisk the tahini with the water, lemon juice, vinegar, cumin, salt and garlic until smooth.
instructions.4: Arrange the eggplant in a baking pan and pour the tahini sauce over.
instructions.5: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 15 minutes.

ec-153.title: Mashed Fried Eggplant with Garlic Yogurt (Beitinjan Mifassakh)
ec-153.culturalNotes: Recipe 153, page 71 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice and salt the eggplants for an hour, then squeeze and pat dry.
instructions.2: Fry them in olive oil until soft and brown.
instructions.3: Mash with the yogurt and garlic.
instructions.4: Stir in the parsley and serve.

ec-154.title: Turkish Eggplant Cream (Hünkar Beğendi)
ec-154.culturalNotes: Recipe 154, page 71 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Roast the eggplants whole in their skins, in a hot oven or on a tray over the stove, turning them when one side softens. Peel, drain and mash the flesh.
instructions.2: Melt the butter and cook the flour in it over a very low heat until golden.
instructions.3: Off the heat, stir in the hot milk, then return to the heat and let it bubble.
instructions.4: Stir in the eggplant, season and cook for 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Off the heat, stir in the cheese and parsley and serve.

ec-155.title: Imam Bayildi with Minced Beef and Yogurt
ec-155.culturalNotes: Recipe 155, page 71 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-155-i6.name: Pine Nuts, Pecans Or Hazelnuts, Chopped

instructions.1: Slice, salt and drain the eggplants, then deep-fry them until dark brown.
instructions.2: Brown the onion in a little oil, add the beef with salt and pepper and cook until its juices are absorbed.
instructions.3: Put the meat and fried eggplant in a pot over a low heat and cook, stirring often, until the eggplant has completely broken down.
instructions.4: Press the mixture against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon to squeeze out excess fat, and pour it off.
instructions.5: Spread in a shallow dish. Mix the yogurt with the garlic and a little salt and spread it over the top.
instructions.6: Sprinkle with the nuts and serve hot or cold.

ec-158.title: Imam Bayildi: Baked Eggplant Shells with Currants
ec-158.culturalNotes: Recipe 158, page 73 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the currants in lukewarm water.
instructions.2: Halve the eggplants lengthwise and scoop out the flesh without piercing the skins. Dice or mash the flesh and sprinkle it with lemon juice.
instructions.3: Fry the eggplant flesh with the onions in the oil, then add the tomatoes, parsley, thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Cover and cook over a low heat for about 20 minutes.
instructions.4: Off the heat, stir in the garlic and the drained currants.
instructions.5: Arrange the eggplant shells in a well-greased baking dish and fill them with the mixture.
instructions.6: Drizzle a little olive oil over each and bake in a slow oven until the shells are soft.

ec-161.title: Poached Fish Sayadiya with Brown Onion Rice (Sayadiyit al-Samak)
ec-161.culturalNotes: Recipe 161, page 74 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Fry the onion in the oil until deep brown.
instructions.2: Add about 2 cups of water with salt and pepper and bring to the boil.
instructions.3: Add the fish and poach over a low heat for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Strain the broth, top it up with water and use it to cook the rice (fry the rice briefly in a little oil first, then simmer until the liquid is absorbed).
instructions.5: Skin, bone and flake the fish and fold it through the rice.

ec-164.title: Fried Fish Sayadiya (Sayadiyit Samak Ma’li)
ec-164.culturalNotes: Recipe 164, page 75 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the fish into neat pieces, fry them and drain on absorbent paper.
instructions.2: Fry the onion in the same oil until deep brown.
instructions.3: Add the rice and water with salt and cook uncovered until the water has been absorbed.
instructions.4: Lay the fried fish on top of the rice, turn the heat to its lowest, cover and cook for 15–20 minutes.
instructions.5: Serve the fish on its rice.

ec-167.title: Fish and Vegetables Baked in Tahini (Samak bi-l-Khudar wi-l-Tahina)
ec-167.culturalNotes: Recipe 167, page 76 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-167-i5.name: Sweet Peppers, Seeded And Thinly Sliced

ec-167-i7.name: Tahini Sauce (tahini Thinned With Water, Lemon, Vinegar, Cumin And Salt)

instructions.1: Cut the fish into large chunks, coat them in seasoned flour and fry. Drain, cool and flake.
instructions.2: Parboil the carrots and slice them thinly.
instructions.3: Sauté the onions and sweet peppers and mix them into the fish with the carrots and eggs.
instructions.4: Spread the mixture in a baking pan and cover it with the tahini sauce.
instructions.5: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 15 minutes.

ec-177.title: Gulf-Style Baked Fish with Tomato and Tamarind (Samak bi Salsat al-Tamata wal-Sabbar)
ec-177.culturalNotes: Recipe 177, page 81 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-177-i3.name: Tamarind (soaked And Strained To 1/2 Cup Concentrate)

instructions.1: Split the fish lengthwise from head to tail and open it out like a book.
instructions.2: Dissolve the tomato paste in the tamarind liquid and set aside.
instructions.3: Blend the garlic, lemon juice, mixed spice and half the fresh coriander. Rub half of this mixture over the fish and leave it to rest.
instructions.4: Lay the fish on an oiled baking tray and bake until cooked through.
instructions.5: Meanwhile, fry the onions and peppers in olive oil until soft, then stir in the ground coriander, cumin, ginger and salt.
instructions.6: Spread the onion mixture and the diced tomatoes over the baked fish, scatter over the remaining coriander and pour the tamarind sauce on top.
instructions.7: Return to the oven for 5–7 minutes so the fish takes on the flavours, then serve.

ec-178.title: Tunisian Breaded Fish in Spicy Tomato Sauce (Hout Moqly)
ec-178.culturalNotes: Recipe 178, page 81 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Marinate the fish in the lemon juice and salt.
instructions.2: Fry the onions and zucchini lightly in olive oil, then add the garlic, harissa, salt, pepper and the tomato paste thinned with 1 cup of water. Cook for 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Mash the sauce and boil it again until reduced and thick.
instructions.4: Dip the fish in beaten egg, coat with breadcrumbs and deep-fry.
instructions.5: Arrange on a serving dish and spoon the tomato sauce over.

ec-179.title: Tunisian Grilled Fish with Eggplant Sauce (Sharmoulit Badinjan)
ec-179.culturalNotes: Recipe 179, page 82 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice, salt and drain the eggplants, then fry them in olive oil until dark brown.
instructions.2: Grill the fish and keep it warm.
instructions.3: Brown the onions in the eggplant oil, add the garlic, harissa, tabil and the tomato paste thinned with 1 cup of water, and cook over a medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring often.
instructions.4: Mash the eggplant with the vinegar and some salt and stir it into the tomato sauce. Cook for 3–5 minutes more.
instructions.5: Pour the sauce over the grilled fish and serve.

ec-180.title: Jordanian Sayadiyeh (Fish in Dark Onion Broth with Rice)
ec-180.culturalNotes: Recipe 180, page 82 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Marinate the fish in the lemon juice and salt for 1–2 hours.
instructions.2: Fry the onions until very brown, then add the garlic and fry, stirring constantly so it does not stick.
instructions.3: Take the pan off the heat and mash the onions well with the back of a spoon. Add the spices, seasoning and plenty of water.
instructions.4: Bring back to the boil, add the fish and cook until tender. The broth should be very dark.
instructions.5: Keep back just enough broth to cover the fish. Fry the rice in oil until every grain is coated, add broth to make 1 1/2 times the volume of the rice, season and cook until tender.
instructions.6: Serve the rice and the fish in its broth separately.

ec-181.title: Iraqi Baked Fish Stuffed with Walnuts and Pomegranate (Samaka Harra)
ec-181.culturalNotes: Recipe 181, page 83 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the bulgur for an hour.
instructions.2: Pound or blend the bulgur with the garlic, onions, walnuts, parsley, coriander, lemon juice and salt until well mixed.
instructions.3: Stir in the pomegranate seeds and stuff the fish with the mixture.
instructions.4: Put the fish and any extra stuffing in a well-oiled baking dish and cover with foil.
instructions.5: Bake in a hot, preheated oven for 30 minutes, then lower to moderate and bake for 30 minutes more.

ec-183.title: Spiced Boiled Gizzards with Mastic (‘Awanis Maslu’a)
ec-183.culturalNotes: Recipe 183, page 84 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Tie the mastic and cardamom in a muslin bag.
instructions.2: Boil 4–5 cups of water with the spice bag, the onion and salt.
instructions.3: Add the gizzards and cook for 10–12 minutes.
instructions.4: Use the gizzards in the dishes that follow, and the broth to cook rice or vermicelli.

ec-184.title: Gizzards and Pearl Onions Baked in Béchamel (‘Awanis bi-l-Bechamel)
ec-184.culturalNotes: Recipe 184, page 84 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Boil the gizzards with mastic, cardamom and onion as in the spiced boiled gizzards recipe.
instructions.2: Peel the pearl onions, leaving them whole, parboil in salted water and drain.
instructions.3: Halve the gizzards and put them in a deep baking dish with the onions.
instructions.4: Stir the nutmeg into the béchamel and pour it over.
instructions.5: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 20 minutes, until the top is browned.

ec-185.title: Gizzard and Vegetable Casserole (Tagin ‘Awanis)
ec-185.culturalNotes: Recipe 185, page 84 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Parboil the carrots, potatoes and peas in salted water and drain. Slice the carrots thinly and dice the potatoes.
instructions.2: Put the vegetables and gizzards in a casserole.
instructions.3: Stir the cornflour and mixed spices into the well-seasoned gizzard broth and pour it over.
instructions.4: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 30–40 minutes.

ec-186.title: Gizzards in Tomato Sauce (‘Awanis bi-l-Dim‘a)
ec-186.culturalNotes: Recipe 186, page 85 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Tomato sauce: soften the onions in oil, add the garlic and fry until pale brown, then add the tomato juice and simmer for 15–20 minutes until dark. Add the vinegar, salt and pepper and cook for 2–3 minutes.
instructions.2: Halve the gizzards and parboil them for 3–5 minutes, then drain.
instructions.3: Add them to the tomato sauce with the mixed spice.
instructions.4: Simmer over a very low heat for 20–30 minutes.

ec-189.title: Freekeh with Gizzards (Firik Matbukh bi-l-‘Awanis)
ec-189.culturalNotes: Recipe 189, page 86 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Clean the freekeh: rub it in a bowl of water so the chaff floats and grit sinks, and rinse until the water runs clear.
instructions.2: Bring the gizzard broth to the boil, topped up with water to make 5 cups.
instructions.3: Add the freekeh and cook for 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Halve the gizzards and mix them into the freekeh.
instructions.5: Pour the melted butter over and cook over a very low heat for 10–15 minutes more, until the freekeh is soft.

ec-191.title: Fried Beef Head Meat (Lahmit al-Ras Ma’liya)
ec-191.culturalNotes: Recipe 191, page 87 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Blanch the meat and drain it (head meat is always sold boned).
instructions.2: Return it to the pot with the chopped onion, peppercorns, salt and just enough water to cover, and cook until tender.
instructions.3: Drain the meat and fry it in the oil.
instructions.4: Strain the stock, thicken it with the cornflour and serve it in a separate bowl.

ec-192.title: Braised Beef Head Meat (Lahmit al-Ras Matbukha)
ec-192.culturalNotes: Recipe 192, page 87 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Rub the onion with salt, pepper and mixed spice.
instructions.2: Put it in a pot with the meat and oil and cook over a very low heat until the meat has reabsorbed the juices it releases.
instructions.3: Add a little water, and more whenever it dries out, and cook until the meat is tender, about 45 minutes.

ec-194.title: Jellied Sheep’s Head Terrine (Jilatin al-Ras)
ec-194.culturalNotes: Recipe 194, page 88 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-194-i9.name: Egg (whole, With Its Crushed Shell, To Clear The Stock)

instructions.1: Have the skull split lengthwise. Soak it in several changes of salted water, singe off any hairs and scrape it with a blunt knife, then wash under running water and blanch.
instructions.2: Remove the brain and keep it for another dish.
instructions.3: Simmer the head over a very low heat for 2–3 hours with the onion, carrot, celery, cardamom, bay leaf, peppercorns, lemon rind and the whole egg (yolk, white and crushed shell).
instructions.4: Strain the stock, season it and set aside.
instructions.5: Cut the meat and tongue into small, even pieces.
instructions.6: Cook the peas and diced carrots in salted water until soft, drain, cool and mix with the chopped pickles.
instructions.7: Line the bottom of a cake mould with meat, cover with the vegetables and finish with another layer of meat.
instructions.8: Pour the stock over and leave to cool. When the jelly has set, turn it out onto a serving dish.

ec-196.title: Braised Heart with Garlic (‘Alb Misabbik)
ec-196.culturalNotes: Recipe 196, page 89 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-196-i2.name: Garlic Cloves, Peeled And Halved Diagonally

instructions.1: Slice the heart and soak it in salted water for 1–2 hours. Rinse in several changes of water, gently squeezing out the blood.
instructions.2: Cook the slices over a low heat, stirring often, until they give up their juice, then drain.
instructions.3: Fry the heart and garlic lightly in the oil and season.
instructions.4: Cover with meat stock and simmer for 30–40 minutes.
instructions.5: In tomato sauce (recipe 197 in the book): use 2–3 cups of tomato sauce instead of the stock.

ec-201.title: Kidneys in Nutmeg Gravy (Kalawi Matbukha)
ec-201.culturalNotes: Recipe 201, page 90 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Remove the skin and fat from the kidneys, cut them into walnut-sized pieces and soak in several changes of salted water for at least an hour. Drain and pat dry.
instructions.2: Sauté the onions in oil, add the kidneys and fry, stirring now and then, until their juices are absorbed.
instructions.3: Add the stock with salt and pepper and cook for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Lift the kidneys onto a warm dish.
instructions.5: Thicken the pan juices with the cornflour, add the nutmeg, check the seasoning and pour over the kidneys.

ec-208.title: Mujaddara (Brown Lentils and Rice with Fried Onions)
ec-208.culturalNotes: Recipe 208, page 94 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cover the lentils with twice their volume of water and boil until almost done.
instructions.2: Add the rice and salt, stir, cover and cook for about 15 minutes, until both lentils and rice are tender.
instructions.3: Fry the onions until deep brown.
instructions.4: Tip the onions and their oil into the lentils, stir and simmer for 5 minutes more.
instructions.5: Serve hot or cold. It should be soft, like a thick porridge.

ec-213.title: Turkish Fried Liver with Spring Onion and Parsley (Ciğer Tava)
ec-213.culturalNotes: Recipe 213, page 95 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the liver in salted water for 30 minutes, drain, pat dry and cut into 3 cm cubes.
instructions.2: Coat the cubes in seasoned flour and fry until nicely browned, taking care not to overcook them.
instructions.3: Season, scatter over the spring onions and parsley and toss together.

ec-214.title: Yemeni Liver and Kidney Stew (Kirsheh)
ec-214.culturalNotes: Recipe 214, page 95 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Wash and skin the kidney, chop it coarsely and soak in several changes of water. Drain and pat dry. Cut the liver into small cubes.
instructions.2: Pound the garlic with the turmeric, cumin, coriander and cardamom into a thick paste.
instructions.3: Fry the kidney in oil, stirring, until its juices have been absorbed or evaporated, then lift it out.
instructions.4: Soften the onions in the same oil, lower the heat right down, add the ginger and garlic paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
instructions.5: Return the kidney, turn up the heat, add the liver and cook for 7–10 minutes, still stirring.
instructions.6: When the liver is browned, add the tomatoes with salt and pepper and cook for about 5 minutes, until the tomatoes are done.

ec-216.title: Beef with Garlic and Coriander (Kuzbariyit al-Lahma)
ec-216.culturalNotes: Recipe 216, page 97 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Crush the garlic with salt and mix it with the coriander.
instructions.2: Cut the beef into small cubes and fry in the oil until it has reabsorbed its juices.
instructions.3: Fry the garlic mixture in a separate pan and add it to the beef.
instructions.4: Season, cover the meat with stock or water and simmer gently for 60–90 minutes.

ec-218.title: Pressed Beef with Onion and Tomato Gravy (Kanduza)
ec-218.culturalNotes: Recipe 218, page 97 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice the beef 2 cm thick and pound to tenderise.
instructions.2: Layer onions, beef and tomatoes in a pot, seasoning each layer lightly.
instructions.3: Weigh the layers down, add 1 cup of water and cook over a low heat for 30–40 minutes.
instructions.4: Take out the beef, fry it in oil and keep it warm on a serving dish.
instructions.5: Blend the vegetables with their juices, strain, and return to the pot.
instructions.6: Season, stir in the cornflour, cook for 2–3 minutes and pour over the beef.

ec-219.title: Garlic-Studded Pot Roast (Lahma Rustu)
ec-219.culturalNotes: Recipe 219, page 98 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Pierce the meat in several places with the tip of a sharp knife.
instructions.2: Roll each garlic clove in salt and pepper and push it into one of the holes.
instructions.3: Brown the meat all over in hot oil.
instructions.4: Add water to come halfway up the meat and cook until tender.
instructions.5: Chill before slicing.

ec-221.title: Cheese and Parsley Beef Rolls in Onion Gravy (Lahma Mahshiya)
ec-221.culturalNotes: Recipe 221, page 98 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice the beef very thinly, cut it into 10 cm squares and pound to tenderise.
instructions.2: Mix the cheeses with the parsley, spread a little on each slice, roll it up and tie with thread.
instructions.3: Put the rolls in a glass or ceramic dish, pour over the blended marinade ingredients and leave for 1–2 hours.
instructions.4: Brush off the marinade (keep it), brown the rolls lightly and arrange them in a baking pan.
instructions.5: Fry the flour in a little oil, take it off the heat and gradually whisk in the strained marinade. Cook for 3–5 minutes and pour over the rolls, adding warm water if the meat is not covered.
instructions.6: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 30 minutes. Snip off the threads before serving.

ec-227.title: Fried Beef and Egg Patties (Kufta bi-l-Beid)
ec-227.culturalNotes: Recipe 227, page 101 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mince the beef, onion and breadcrumbs together twice, or pound them until smooth.
instructions.2: Beat the eggs with salt and pepper and work them into the meat.
instructions.3: Shape into round patties 5–7 cm across and 2 cm thick.
instructions.4: Fry in oil until browned on both sides and cooked through.

ec-228.title: Garlic Meatballs in Sweet-Sour Tomato Sauce (Kufta bi-l-Toom wi-l-Bassal)
ec-228.culturalNotes: Recipe 228, page 101 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mince the beef, onion and garlic together twice, or pound until smooth. Season and mix.
instructions.2: Shape into small balls and fry.
instructions.3: Dissolve the vinegar and sugar in the tomato juice and cook for 3–5 minutes.
instructions.4: Drop in the meatballs and simmer for 30 minutes, shaking the pot gently now and then so they do not stick.
instructions.5: Thicken the sauce with the cornflour.

ec-229.title: Leek Meatballs in Lemon Broth (Kufta bi-l-Kurrat)
ec-229.culturalNotes: Recipe 229, page 102 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Boil the leeks in salted water until tender and drain.
instructions.2: Mince the beef and leeks together twice, then mix in the beaten eggs, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Shape into small balls and fry.
instructions.4: Bring 2 cups of water to the boil with 1 tablespoon of oil and the lemon juice.
instructions.5: Slip in the meatballs and simmer for about 30 minutes, shaking the pot gently so they do not stick.

ec-236.title: Lamb Stew with Crisp Potato Fingers (Lahma Dani Matbukha)
ec-236.culturalNotes: Recipe 236, page 105 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Peel the tomato, garlic and onion.
instructions.2: Cook the meat with the whole vegetables in oil over a very low heat until the juices have been reabsorbed.
instructions.3: Cover with warm water, season and cook over a very low heat for about an hour, until tender.
instructions.4: Lift the meat onto a serving dish and keep warm.
instructions.5: Mash the vegetables into the broth until smooth, bring it to the boil and toss in the fried potatoes. Cook for 3–5 minutes.
instructions.6: Pour over the meat and serve hot.

ec-238.title: Braised Veal Shin with Straw Potatoes (Moza Matbukha)
ec-238.culturalNotes: Recipe 238, page 106 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes and slice the onions coarsely.
instructions.2: Sauté the onions in oil, add the meat and brown it all over.
instructions.3: Cover with warm water, season and cook over a very low heat for about an hour.
instructions.4: Cut the peeled potatoes into matchsticks, fry until very crisp and drain on absorbent paper.
instructions.5: When the meat is ready, add the potatoes and cook for about 10 minutes so they soak up the juices.

ec-243.title: Tunisian Lamb and Parsley Tajine (Tajine Ma’doones)
ec-243.culturalNotes: Recipe 243, page 110 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the beans overnight, then boil them in fresh water for 20–30 minutes. Drain, keeping the liquid.
instructions.2: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes and roll them in salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Soften the onions in olive oil, add the lamb and fry until its juices have been reabsorbed.
instructions.4: Add the cayenne, beans, tabil and the tomato paste dissolved in enough bean liquid to just cover the lamb. Cook until the lamb and beans are tender, then take off the heat.
instructions.5: Beat the eggs with the parsley, breadcrumbs, cheese and seasoning and stir them thoroughly into the lamb.
instructions.6: Pour into a well-greased ovenproof dish and bake in a moderate oven for 15–20 minutes, until set.

ec-244.title: Tunisian Lamb and Mint Tajine (Tajine Na‘na‘)
ec-244.culturalNotes: Recipe 244, page 110 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the lamb into bite-sized pieces and roll them in salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Fry the onions in ghee until golden, add the lamb and brown it until its juices are reabsorbed.
instructions.3: Stir in the tomatoes, tabil and seasoning and cook over a low heat for 30 minutes, adding hot water if the meat is not covered.
instructions.4: Drain the meat, keeping the broth, and put it in a greased casserole.
instructions.5: Beat the eggs with the cheese, mint, breadcrumbs and seasoning, mix in the meat and 1 cup of the broth, and pour back into the casserole.
instructions.6: Bake in a moderate oven for 20 minutes.

ec-245.title: Cypriot Tava (Lamb and Tomato Slow-Baked with Cumin)
ec-245.culturalNotes: Recipe 245, page 111 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes.
instructions.2: Thin the tomato paste with 1/2 cup of warm water and put it in a casserole with all the other ingredients.
instructions.3: Close with a tight-fitting lid and bake in a moderate oven for 2–3 hours, until the lamb is tender and the sauce has thickened.

ec-246.title: Tunisian Lamb and Potato Meatballs (Kabaar)
ec-246.culturalNotes: Recipe 246, page 111 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Boil the potatoes until very soft, then peel and mash them.
instructions.2: Mince the lamb twice with the onions, garlic, parsley, coriander, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Mix in the mashed potato, breadcrumbs, cinnamon and well-beaten eggs.
instructions.4: Shape into small balls and chill for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: Fry in very hot oil until browned all over.

ec-247.title: Baked Kofta Rolls with Pine Nuts (Kafta Mabroomeh / Mkabtaleh)
ec-247.culturalNotes: Recipe 247, page 112 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mince the meat twice with the onions, garlic, salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Beat the eggs, add them to the meat and knead well.
instructions.3: Roll the meat out about 1 cm thick on a lightly greased surface and cut it into rounds.
instructions.4: Put a few pine nuts in the middle of each round and roll it up.
instructions.5: Arrange the rolls on a well-greased tray and brush each with fat.
instructions.6: Bake in the middle of a moderate oven for 30 minutes, then brown under the grill, shaking the tray so they colour evenly.

ec-248.title: Lebanese Kafta Fatteh with Garlic Yogurt (Fatteet Kafta Madqooqa)
ec-248.culturalNotes: Recipe 248, page 112 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mince the lamb twice with the fresh mint, salt and pepper, and shape into patties.
instructions.2: Fry the patties until nicely browned.
instructions.3: Break the bread into bite-sized pieces and put them in a deep serving bowl.
instructions.4: Mix the yogurt with the garlic and dried mint, then stir in the oil left from frying the patties.
instructions.5: Pour the yogurt over the bread and top with the kafta.

ec-249.title: Izmir Meatballs in Tomato Sauce (İzmir Köftesi)
ec-249.culturalNotes: Recipe 249, page 113 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-249-i10.name: Sauce: Sweet Green Pepper, Very Finely Diced

instructions.1: Sprinkle the bread with cold water and squeeze it out.
instructions.2: Mince the bread twice with the beef, onions, parsley, garlic, cumin, salt and pepper, then knead in the egg.
instructions.3: With wet hands, shape round or oval balls and roll them very lightly in seasoned flour.
instructions.4: Fry the meatballs lightly and drain them on absorbent paper.
instructions.5: Soften the green pepper in the same oil, add the tomato juice, sugar, salt and pepper and cook for 10–12 minutes.
instructions.6: Return the meatballs and simmer for 30 minutes, until the sauce thickens.

ec-261.title: Upper Egyptian Mashed Okra with Beef and Chili (Bamya Weeka Sa‘idi)
ec-261.culturalNotes: Recipe 261, page 118 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the beef into small cubes and boil it in the stock for 20–30 minutes, until tender. Lift it out.
instructions.2: Add the okra and chilies to the broth, cook for about 10 minutes, then mash with a fork.
instructions.3: Return the meat to the pot.
instructions.4: Make the ta’liya: pound the garlic with the coriander, salt and pepper and fry it in the oil for 3–5 minutes. Tip it into the pot, swirl a spoonful of broth round the frying pan and add that too.
instructions.5: Simmer for 5–7 minutes and serve.

ec-265.title: Iraqi Okra Stew with Tamarind (Bamia Marag)
ec-265.culturalNotes: Recipe 265, page 119 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-265-i7.name: Cumin, Coriander, Cinnamon, Cloves And Peppercorns

instructions.1: Cut the mutton into bite-sized cubes and boil with the spices until tender. Lift it out, keeping the broth.
instructions.2: Fry the mutton in ghee, then add the okra and garlic and stir until everything is well fried.
instructions.3: Dissolve the tomato paste in the tamarind liquid, season, and add it to the pot with the broth.
instructions.4: Simmer for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: Take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice.

ec-266.title: Oven-Roasted Pearl Onions (’Awirma Mashwiya)
ec-266.culturalNotes: Recipe 266, page 120 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Put the onions, still in their skins, in a hot oven for about an hour, until thoroughly cooked.
instructions.2: Peel them at the table; they should be soft enough to melt in the mouth.

ec-267.title: Pearl Onion and Beef Casserole (Tagin ’Awirma)
ec-267.culturalNotes: Recipe 267, page 120 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the beef into small cubes. Peel the garlic and halve it diagonally.
instructions.2: Fry the beef and onions lightly in oil and move them to a casserole.
instructions.3: Add the garlic, mixed spice, salt and pepper and cover with the stock.
instructions.4: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 90–120 minutes.
instructions.5: Thicken the gravy with cornflour if you like.
instructions.6: Sweet-sour version (recipe 268 in the book): use 2 cups of tomato juice instead of stock, with 1 teaspoon each of sugar and vinegar dissolved in it, and spice with cinnamon or nutmeg.

ec-271.title: Meat-Filled Gullash Fingers (Asabi‘ Gullash bi-l-Lahma)
ec-271.culturalNotes: Recipe 271, page 122 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Make the savory minced beef: fry the onion in a little oil until pale gold, add the beef, salt and pepper and cook until the juices are absorbed. You need about 1 cup.
instructions.2: Cut the gullash into 10 cm squares and keep them under a cloth so they do not dry out.
instructions.3: Working one square at a time, lay a narrow strip of meat across the middle, stopping 1 cm from each end.
instructions.4: Fold in the ends and roll up very tightly.
instructions.5: Pack the fingers into a greased baking pan and brush the tops with melted butter.
instructions.6: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven until golden.

ec-273.title: Crisp Layered Ruqaq with Cheese and Egg (Saniyit Ru’a’ bi-l-Gibna)
ec-273.culturalNotes: Recipe 273, page 123 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Grate the Balkan cheese. Mash the areesh cheese with the hard-boiled eggs, then mix in the grated cheese, the beaten raw egg and a pinch of pepper.
instructions.2: Grease a deep baking pan (you will need a second pan the same size). Dip one ruqaq sheet at a time in hot broth and use them to line the pan, sprinkling each layer with a little oil.
instructions.3: After 3–4 layers, spread the cheese filling evenly, then carry on with more dipped, oiled layers.
instructions.4: Pour any remaining oil over the top and bake in a moderate oven.
instructions.5: When the top is brown, turn it over into the second pan and return it to the oven to brown the other side.
instructions.6: Cut into pieces while hot.

ec-275.title: Lamb and Lisan ‘Asfur Pasta Casserole (Tagin Lisan ‘Asfur)
ec-275.culturalNotes: Recipe 275, page 124 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Seed the peppers and slice them thinly.
instructions.2: Sauté the onion in the butter and oil, add the lamb and fry until its juices are absorbed.
instructions.3: Cover with stock, add the peppers, cinnamon, salt and pepper and cook for 15–20 minutes.
instructions.4: Lift out the meat and vegetables with a slotted spoon and put them in an ovenproof pot.
instructions.5: Parboil the lisan ‘asfur in the stock for 5–7 minutes and pour it over the meat, adding hot water if it is not covered.
instructions.6: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 30 minutes.

ec-281.title: Shishbarak (Meat Dumplings in Garlic Yogurt)
ec-281.culturalNotes: Recipe 281, page 127 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Sift the flour with salt and add enough water to knead a smooth dough that comes away from the bowl. Rest it for an hour.
instructions.2: Fry the pine nuts golden and set aside. Soften the onion in the same oil, add the meat and fry until its juices are gone, then stir in the pine nuts, spices, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Roll the dough out on a floured surface and cut it into small rounds.
instructions.4: Put 1/2 teaspoon of filling on each, fold into a crescent with wet fingers, then wrap it round your finger and pinch the ends together so it looks like a little hat.
instructions.5: Set them on a greased tray, brush with ghee and bake in a moderate oven until crisp and golden.
instructions.6: Fry the garlic in a little ghee until golden, stirring constantly, and stir in the mint.
instructions.7: Whisk the egg whites until frothy and mix them into the yogurt to keep it from splitting. Heat it uncovered over a low heat and add the garlic mixture.
instructions.8: When the yogurt bubbles, add the shishbarak and cook for 7–10 minutes more.

ec-283.title: Layered Peas, Rice and Minced Beef Béchamel (Basilla bi-l-Bechamel)
ec-283.culturalNotes: Recipe 283, page 128 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Parboil the peas in salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
instructions.2: Grease a deep ovenproof serving dish, preferably glass.
instructions.3: Arrange the rice, peas and minced beef in several thin layers, moistening every layer with béchamel.
instructions.4: Pour the beaten egg over the top.
instructions.5: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 20–30 minutes, until browned on top.

ec-308.title: Brown Onion Rice for Fish (Ruzz Ahmar)
ec-308.culturalNotes: Recipe 308, page 137 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the rice in warm water for 15–20 minutes and drain.
instructions.2: Fry the onions in the oil until deep brown.
instructions.3: Add the water and salt and bring to the boil.
instructions.4: Stir in the rice, cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 15–20 minutes.
instructions.5: For a redder rice (recipe 309 in the book), stir 1 tablespoon of tomato paste into the water before adding the rice.

ec-310.title: Rice Cooked in Shrimp Stock (Ruzz bi-Salsit Gambari)
ec-310.culturalNotes: Recipe 310, page 138 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Rinse the shrimp under running water until it runs clear. Put them in a pot with the onions, lemons, cumin, salt and pepper, without any water, and cook over a moderate heat, tossing every few minutes, for about 7 minutes or until done.
instructions.2: Cool and shell the shrimp, keeping the heads, shells and juices. Remove the dark vein.
instructions.3: Make the shrimp sauce: blend the heads, shells and juices at high speed and strain. You need 1 cup.
instructions.4: Fry the rice in the oil, stirring until every grain is coated.
instructions.5: Add 2 cups of water and the cup of shrimp sauce. It is already well seasoned, so add no salt.
instructions.6: Cook uncovered over a moderate heat until the liquid is absorbed, then cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 20–30 minutes.
instructions.7: Serve with the shrimp.

ec-311.title: Rice with Tomatoes, Peppers and Carrots (Ruzz bi-l-Khudar)
ec-311.culturalNotes: Recipe 311, page 138 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-311-i4.name: Sweet Green Peppers, Blanched And Thinly Sliced

instructions.1: Sauté the onion until golden and mix it with the tomatoes, peppers and carrots.
instructions.2: Fry the rice in the same oil, stirring, until every grain is coated.
instructions.3: Add the vegetables, water, salt and pepper and stir one last time.
instructions.4: Cook uncovered over a high heat until the water is absorbed.
instructions.5: Cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 15–20 minutes.

ec-313.title: Soft Rice Porridge with Beef (Ruzz Lubba bi-l-Lahma)
ec-313.culturalNotes: Recipe 313, page 139 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes.
instructions.2: Fry the onions until golden, add the beef and fry over a high heat until its juices are absorbed.
instructions.3: Season, add water to cover and cook over a low heat for 15–20 minutes.
instructions.4: Top up the water to 4–5 cups, stir in the rice and check the seasoning.
instructions.5: Cover and cook slowly for about 30 minutes. It should end up soft and porridge-like.
instructions.6: With gizzards (recipe 314 in the book): stir 5–6 mastic grains into hot oil for 10–15 seconds, add halved boiled gizzards, cover and turn off the heat for 1–2 minutes, then fry them, add 4 cups of water and the rice and cook the same way.

ec-315.title: Turkish Eggplant Pilaf (Patlıcanlı Pilav)
ec-315.culturalNotes: Recipe 315, page 140 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Dice the eggplant without peeling, salt it and leave for an hour. Squeeze out the moisture and pat dry.
instructions.2: Fry the eggplant until lightly browned and drain on absorbent paper.
instructions.3: Soften the chopped onion in the same oil, then add the tomatoes, parsley, mint, eggplant, salt and pepper and bring to the boil.
instructions.4: Add the rice and enough water to cover.
instructions.5: Boil hard, then lower the heat and simmer gently for 30 minutes.

ec-317.title: Saffron Rice Kibbeh (Kubbat Halab)
ec-317.culturalNotes: Recipe 317, page 141 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-317-i5.name: Celery Or Parsley, Very Finely Chopped

instructions.1: Boil the rice in 4 cups of water with the saffron and salt until soft, breaking up any lumps with a fork. Drain off any water left.
instructions.2: Add the lightly beaten egg and, with fingers dipped in the turmeric rose water, knead the rice into a soft dough that holds its shape.
instructions.3: Filling: fry the beef, then add the celery or parsley, almonds, raisins, mixed spice, salt and pepper and cook together over a low heat for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Take a little rice dough in your palm, moistened with rose water, and hollow it out with a finger of the other hand, turning it into a thin cup.
instructions.5: Fill with the meat, close it into an oval ball with a moistened palm and set it on a floured surface. Repeat until the dough is used up.
instructions.6: Deep-fry in ghee until golden.

ec-318.title: Persian Crusty Steamed Rice with Yogurt Tahdig (Chelow Dig)
ec-318.culturalNotes: Recipe 318, page 141 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Wash the rice in boiling water and drain.
instructions.2: Bring 8 cups of heavily salted water to the boil, add the rice, cook for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse in hot water.
instructions.3: Stir the yogurt into one cup of the half-cooked rice.
instructions.4: Swirl a tablespoon of ghee round the base and sides of a heavy pan and spread the yogurt rice over the bottom.
instructions.5: Pile the rest of the rice on top, sprinkle with the remaining ghee and steam over a moderate heat, breaking up any clusters, until tender and crusty underneath.
instructions.6: Mound the steamed rice in the middle of a dish and break the golden crust from the bottom of the pan into pieces around it.

ec-320.title: Everyday Egyptian Salad Dressing (Khalta li-l-Salata)
ec-320.culturalNotes: Recipe 320, page 142 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mix all the ingredients together.
instructions.2: Pour over the salad just before serving.

ec-323.title: Fresh Cabbage Salad with Garlic and Lemon (Salatit Krumb)
ec-323.culturalNotes: Recipe 323, page 143 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Sprinkle the cabbage and onion with salt and rub well, then rinse and drain.
instructions.2: Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic and salt.
instructions.3: Pour over the vegetables and toss.

ec-329.title: Egyptian Chopped Salad (Salata Baladi)
ec-329.culturalNotes: Recipe 329, page 145 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-329-i11.name: Salad Dressing (oil, Lemon, Vinegar, Salt And Pepper)

instructions.1: Only onions and tomatoes are essential; add whatever else the season offers.
instructions.2: Chop everything finely, keeping each vegetable separate.
instructions.3: Rub the onion with salt, rinse it and leave it to soak in lemon juice.
instructions.4: Rub the inside of the salad bowl with the cut garlic clove and heap the vegetables in it.
instructions.5: Just before serving, add the dressing and toss.

ec-331.title: Artichoke and Egg Salad (Salatit Kharshuf)
ec-331.culturalNotes: Recipe 331, page 146 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-331-i3.name: Salad Dressing (oil, Lemon, Vinegar, Salt And Pepper)

instructions.1: Boil the artichoke hearts in salted water until tender, drain and chop.
instructions.2: Add them to the chopped eggs.
instructions.3: Pour over the dressing and mix well.

ec-332.title: Green Bean Salad with Red Onion (Salatit Fasulya Khadra)
ec-332.culturalNotes: Recipe 332, page 146 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: String the beans and trim the tops and tails.
instructions.2: Boil in salted water until tender, drain and spread out to cool.
instructions.3: Put the sliced onion in the salad bowl to soak in the lemon juice.
instructions.4: Before serving, add the beans and oil and mix.

ec-333.title: Beetroot Salad with Garlic Vinegar (Salatit Bangar bi-l-Toom)
ec-333.culturalNotes: Recipe 333, page 146 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Boil the beetroot for about an hour, until very tender.
instructions.2: Drain, keeping two tablespoons of the cooking water. Cool, peel and cut into small cubes, thin slices or fingers.
instructions.3: Crush the garlic with salt until very smooth and mix in the vinegar.
instructions.4: Stir the garlic dressing into the reserved cooking water, pour over the beetroot and mix gently.
instructions.5: With tahini (recipe 334 in the book): dress the beetroot with 2 tablespoons of thin tahini sauce instead.
instructions.6: With yogurt (recipe 335 in the book): mix the cubed beetroot with 3 diced tomatoes and 3–5 diced cucumbers and cover with 1 cup of garlic yogurt (yogurt, crushed garlic and salt, without mint).

ec-336.title: Blanched Cabbage Salad with Salted Fish (Salatit Krumb)
ec-336.culturalNotes: Recipe 336, page 147 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-336-i3.name: Salad Dressing (oil, Lemon, Vinegar, Salt And Pepper)

instructions.1: Shred the cabbage very finely, blanch it for 1 minute, drain and cool.
instructions.2: Chop the fish very finely and stir it into the dressing.
instructions.3: Pour over the cabbage and mix well.

ec-337.title: Wilted Spinach Salad with Onion and Lemon (Salatit Sabanikh)
ec-337.culturalNotes: Recipe 337, page 147 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Chop the spinach leaves and stems coarsely, sprinkle with salt and rub until they lose some juice. Rinse and pat dry.
instructions.2: Wilt the spinach over a low heat, drain and spread out to cool.
instructions.3: Mix in the onion, lemon juice, oil and salt.

ec-338.title: Turkish Spinach Salad with Feta (Ispanak Salatası)
ec-338.culturalNotes: Recipe 338, page 147 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Rinse the spinach, chop it coarsely and wilt it in a pot over the heat.
instructions.2: Drain in a colander, pressing with a spoon to squeeze out the moisture, and put it in a bowl.
instructions.3: Fry the onions in the olive oil until golden and add them to the bowl.
instructions.4: Add the parsley, cheese, salt and pepper and toss well.

ec-342.title: Brown Onion Sauce (Salsa Bunniya)
ec-342.culturalNotes: Recipe 342, page 149 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Melt the butter with the oil over a low heat and fry the onion until deep brown. Lift the onion out and set aside.
instructions.2: Stir the flour into the fat until well blended and cook it.
instructions.3: Add the stock a little at a time, stirring constantly, until you have a smooth, thin cream.
instructions.4: Return the onion, season, and cook on, adding more stock for a thin, smooth sauce.

ec-344.title: Dried Kishk Cakes for Storing (Kishk li-l-Takhzin)
ec-344.culturalNotes: Recipe 344, page 150 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Dissolve the salt in the milk.
instructions.2: Gradually work in the sifted flour until you have a thick dough that comes cleanly away from the bowl.
instructions.3: Leave it to ferment for 4–5 days, sprinkling flour over the top.
instructions.4: Shape it into small, flat round cakes and dry them in the open air for a few days, turning each cake twice a day, until very hard.
instructions.5: Store in a tightly closed box, as cakes or pounded to a powder, ready to cook into kishk.
instructions.6: With yogurt (recipe 345 in the book): make it the same way with yogurt instead of milk. As yogurt is already fermented it needs only 2–3 days, and the taste is quite different.
instructions.7: Upper Egyptian kishk (recipe 346 in the book): rinse fine bulgur and spread it to dry, then cover it with salted soured milk in a large earthenware pot for 5 days, adding more soured milk every 24 hours. On the sixth day knead it into a stiff dough, shape small round cakes and dry them the same way.

ec-353.title: Cypriot Garlic and Almond Sauce (Skordalia)
ec-353.culturalNotes: Recipe 353, page 152 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Sprinkle the bread with water, squeeze it out and crumble it into a bowl.
instructions.2: Soak the garlic in the vinegar for 10 minutes, then add it to the bread with the almonds, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Beat in the lemon juice and oil alternately, in thin streams, until the sauce is as thick as custard.

ec-354.title: Turkish Hazelnut Tarator Sauce
ec-354.culturalNotes: Recipe 354, page 153 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Sprinkle the bread with water, squeeze it out and crumble it into a bowl. Add the hazelnuts and garlic.
instructions.2: Beat in the vinegar, salt and oil alternately, in a thin stream, until the sauce is like a thin custard.
instructions.3: Chill before using.
instructions.4: Hazelnuts are the original, but a mix of pine nuts, almonds and/or walnuts is also used, in which case use lemon juice instead of vinegar.

ec-355.title: Gulf Spiced Onion Sauce for Grilled Meat (Sharmoola)
ec-355.culturalNotes: Recipe 355, page 153 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Heat the oil and cook the ginger, saffron, cumin and hot pepper in it for 1–2 minutes.
instructions.2: Lower the heat and add the onions, salt, garlic, parsley and coriander.
instructions.3: Cook, stirring constantly, until everything is soft and well blended.

ec-356.title: Cypriot Tomato Sauce with Cinnamon and Bay (Saltsa Tomata)
ec-356.culturalNotes: Recipe 356, page 154 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Fry the onion until golden, add the tomatoes and cook for 3–5 minutes.
instructions.2: Thin the tomato paste with an equal amount of water and add it with the sugar, bay leaf, cinnamon, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Cook uncovered for 20 minutes, until thick.
instructions.4: Remove the bay leaf and cinnamon before using.

ec-361.title: Crabs Steamed with Lemon and Onion (Kaburya)
ec-361.culturalNotes: Recipe 361, page 156 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Wash the crabs under running water.
instructions.2: Put everything in a pot, without any water, over a low heat.
instructions.3: Toss from time to time; depending on their size the crabs should be done in 7–10 minutes.
instructions.4: Eat them just as they are: crack the shells of the body and legs and pick out the meat.

ec-364.title: Cumin Batter-Fried Baby Shrimp (Gambari Ma’li)
ec-364.culturalNotes: Recipe 364, page 157 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Wash the shrimp well and peel them.
instructions.2: Mix the flour, milk, water, egg and cumin into a thin batter.
instructions.3: Dip the shrimp in the batter and deep-fry in very hot oil.
instructions.4: Drain on absorbent paper and sprinkle with salt and cumin.

ec-366.title: Egyptian Chicken Soup with Mastic and Cardamom (Shurbit Firakh)
ec-366.culturalNotes: Recipe 366, page 158 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Tie the cardamom and mastic in a muslin bag.
instructions.2: Bring 3 cups of water to the boil with the onions and spice bag.
instructions.3: Lower in the chicken, season and turn down the heat.
instructions.4: When the chicken is tender, lift it out, discard the spice bag and mash the onion into the broth.
instructions.5: Add the rice or vermicelli and cook for 12–15 minutes.
instructions.6: Palestinian version (recipe 367 in the book): just before serving, add 1–2 tablespoons of pine nuts and 1/2 cup of parsley leaves and heat without boiling.

ec-373.title: Turkish Wedding Soup (Düğün Çorbası)
ec-373.culturalNotes: Recipe 373, page 160 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes, roll them in seasoned flour and fry.
instructions.2: Add the lamb to the broth, bring to the boil and add the carrot, onion and seasoning. Simmer for about an hour.
instructions.3: Lift out the meat, keep back one ladleful of soup to cool, and mash the vegetables into the rest. Return the meat and keep the soup over a very low heat.
instructions.4: Beat the egg yolks with the lemon juice, then beat in the cooled ladleful of soup.
instructions.5: Stir the egg mixture into the soup and heat for 2–3 minutes. Do not let it boil or the eggs will curdle.

ec-374.title: Tunisian Fish and Barley Soup (Chorba bil Hout)
ec-374.culturalNotes: Recipe 374, page 160 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-374-i2.name: Fish Head, Backbone, Tail And Trimmings

ec-374-i8.name: Celery Leaves And Stalks, Coarsely Chopped

instructions.1: Cover the fish head, bones and trimmings with water and bring to the boil, skimming as needed.
instructions.2: Boil the barley in salted water for 30 minutes, drain and keep warm.
instructions.3: Fry the fillets lightly and set them aside. Soften the onions in the same oil, add the tomato paste and stir for 2–3 minutes.
instructions.4: Add this to the fish stock with the garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, parsley, celery, salt and pepper and boil for 20 minutes.
instructions.5: Let it cool, remove the fish pieces, blend the liquid and strain it through a very fine sieve, ideally lined with muslin.
instructions.6: Return to the pot with the barley and fish fillets, check the seasoning and boil for 7–10 minutes, until the fish is cooked.
instructions.7: Add the lemon juice and serve.

ec-376.title: Gulf Mutton, Chickpea and Vermicelli Soup (Tchorba)
ec-376.culturalNotes: Recipe 376, page 162 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas in water overnight.
instructions.2: Fry the cutlets in ghee, then add everything except the vermicelli, cover with twice their volume of water and cook until tender.
instructions.3: Take out the cutlets, mash the vegetables and return the cutlets to the pot.
instructions.4: When the soup boils, check the seasoning, add the vermicelli and cook for 10 minutes more, until it is tender and has taken on the flavour of the soup.

ec-377.title: Tunisian Hlalem Noodle Soup with Lamb and Vegetables
ec-377.culturalNotes: Recipe 377, page 162 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas and fava beans for a few hours. Drain, then boil with the onion in twice their volume of water for 15 minutes. Set aside with their liquid.
instructions.2: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes and fry in olive oil. Add the scallions and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
instructions.3: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 5 minutes, then add the spinach, celery, parsley, artichokes, carrots, paprika, salt and pepper and stir until coated.
instructions.4: Add the chickpeas and beans with their liquid and simmer for 30–45 minutes. Cool and skim off any excess fat.
instructions.5: About an hour before serving, bring back to the boil, adding more salted water if needed, then add the hlalem and sweet peppers. Cover and simmer until the noodles are plump and soft.
instructions.6: Add the peas, check the seasoning and sprinkle with fresh coriander.

ec-380.title: Egyptian Chickpea Soup with Cumin and Lemon (Shurbit Hummus)
ec-380.culturalNotes: Recipe 380, page 164 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight and drain.
instructions.2: Cover with twice their volume of fresh water, add the onions and cook for 20–30 minutes, until tender.
instructions.3: Add the cumin, lemon juice, salt and pepper and boil for 3–5 minutes more.
instructions.4: Serve with croutons of baladi bread.

ec-381.title: Thick Chickpea Soup over Bread (Shurbit Hummus)
ec-381.culturalNotes: Recipe 381, page 164 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight and drain.
instructions.2: Cook them with the onions in twice their volume of fresh water for 20–30 minutes. Keep back one cup of the broth.
instructions.3: Add the garlic, cumin and lemon juice to the chickpeas and blend or mash into a thin paste.
instructions.4: Return to the heat, add the oil, season, and cook for 3–5 minutes.
instructions.5: Cut the bread into 2–3 cm pieces and line the serving dish with them.
instructions.6: Reheat the reserved broth, moisten the bread with it and pour the chickpea soup over.

ec-383.title: Tunisian Lablabi (Garlicky Chickpea Soup over Bread)
ec-383.culturalNotes: Recipe 383, page 165 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight and drain.
instructions.2: Boil them in fresh water with the onion and marrow bone until tender. Shake the marrow into the soup and mash it with the onion. Season.
instructions.3: Fry the garlic and harissa in olive oil, stirring constantly so they do not stick.
instructions.4: Add the chickpeas and broth and cook for 5 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and cumin.
instructions.5: Put bite-sized pieces of bread in a serving bowl, pour the soup over and serve at once.

ec-384.title: Cypriot Brown Lentil Soup with Vinegar (Fakes Xidati)
ec-384.culturalNotes: Recipe 384, page 166 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Put the lentils, spring onions, garlic, oil and parsley in a large pot with twice their volume of water and boil until tender.
instructions.2: Season and keep at a gentle simmer.
instructions.3: Mix the cornflour with a tablespoon of cold water and stir it into the boiling soup to thicken it.
instructions.4: Just before serving, check the seasoning and stir in the vinegar.

ec-388.title: Creamy Zucchini Soup (Shurbit Kosa)
ec-388.culturalNotes: Recipe 388, page 168 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Peel the zucchini and chop coarsely.
instructions.2: Boil in the stock for about 5 minutes, until tender.
instructions.3: Mash or blend, then add the milk.
instructions.4: Reheat uncovered with salt over a low heat for 3–5 minutes.

ec-389.title: Turkish Hot Yogurt Soup (Yoğurt Çorbası)
ec-389.culturalNotes: Recipe 389, page 168 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soften the onions in the oil.
instructions.2: Bring the broth to the boil, add the onions and simmer for about 10 minutes.
instructions.3: Take off the heat and pour in the yogurt gradually, stirring constantly.
instructions.4: Return to the heat just until it reaches boiling point, then take off, add salt and sprinkle with coriander.

ec-390.title: Persian Yogurt Soup with Fenugreek and Walnuts (Eshkeneh Shirazi)
ec-390.culturalNotes: Recipe 390, page 169 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Grind the fenugreek to a powder.
instructions.2: Fry the onions until golden, add the flour and cook over a very low heat until well blended.
instructions.3: Add the walnuts and fenugreek with 1/2 cup of hot water and stir until smooth.
instructions.4: Add 2 cups of hot water, season and simmer for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: Beat a ladle of the hot soup into the yogurt, then stir the yogurt into the soup over the heat and take it off before it boils.

ec-398.title: Turkish Spinach with Garlic Yogurt (Ispanak Kavurması)
ec-398.culturalNotes: Recipe 398, page 172 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Wilt the spinach in a pot over a low heat, then drain in a colander, pressing out all the moisture.
instructions.2: Fry the onions in the olive oil until pale brown.
instructions.3: Add the spinach with salt and pepper and cook for 10 minutes, then move to a serving bowl.
instructions.4: Mix the yogurt with the garlic, stir it into the spinach and serve cold.

ec-399.title: Persian Spinach with Lentils (Shuleh Qalamkar)
ec-399.culturalNotes: Recipe 399, page 172 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Wilt the spinach in a pot over a low heat and drain it in a colander, pressing out all the moisture.
instructions.2: Boil the lentils until tender, drain and mix them into the spinach.
instructions.3: Melt the butter, add the vegetables, garlic, spices, salt and pepper and cook for 5–7 minutes.

ec-402.title: Tomato and Beef Stew with Cardamom (Yakhnit Tamatim)
ec-402.culturalNotes: Recipe 402, page 173 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-402-i1.name: Ripe Tomatoes, Peeled And Coarsely Chopped

instructions.1: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes. Tie the cardamom and bay leaf in a muslin bag.
instructions.2: Cook the beef in a little water with the spice bag, onions, salt and pepper for about 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Discard the bag and mash the onions.
instructions.4: Add the tomatoes and mixed spice and simmer for 20–30 minutes.
instructions.5: Garlic version (recipe 403 in the book): cook the tomatoes with 10–12 crushed garlic cloves instead of the bay leaf and cardamom.

ec-404.title: Turkish Green Tomato Gratin (Yeşil Domates Graten)
ec-404.culturalNotes: Recipe 404, page 174 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soften the onions in olive oil and spread them over the bottom of an ovenproof dish.
instructions.2: Slice the tomatoes thickly and lay them on the onions.
instructions.3: Mix the stock with the rest of the oil, season and pour over.
instructions.4: Cover with foil and bake in a slow oven until the tomatoes are tender.
instructions.5: Mash the vegetables, check the seasoning, stir in the cheese and brown the top under the grill.

ec-414.title: Cypriot Oven-Baked Vegetables (Briami)
ec-414.culturalNotes: Recipe 414, page 179 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-414-i2.name: Zucchini, Peeled And Sliced Into Rounds

ec-414-i3.name: Green Sweet Peppers, Seeded And Chopped

instructions.1: Fry the onions lightly until golden, add the peppers and cook for 5 minutes.
instructions.2: Grease an ovenproof dish and add all the ingredients.
instructions.3: Cover and bake in a moderate oven until all the vegetables are very tender.

ec-415.title: Levantine Eggplant and Chickpea Stew (Mnazzaleh)
ec-415.culturalNotes: Recipe 415, page 179 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight and drain.
instructions.2: Peel and slice the eggplants, salt them and leave for about an hour. Squeeze out the moisture, pat dry, deep-fry and drain on absorbent paper.
instructions.3: Fry the onions until dark in the same oil, then add the tomatoes, garlic and chickpeas and cook for about 20 minutes, until the chickpeas are tender, adding hot water if needed.
instructions.4: Add the fried eggplant, a tablespoon each of parsley and coriander, the mint and the nutmeg or cinnamon. Season and simmer for 10 minutes more.
instructions.5: Let it cool and serve warm, topped with the rest of the herbs.

ec-424.title: Turkish Yogurt Kebab on Toast (Yoğurtlu Kebap)
ec-424.culturalNotes: Recipe 424, page 184 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes and marinate them in the onions, lemon juice and salt for at least an hour.
instructions.2: Brush off the marinade and fry the lamb slowly until tender. Keep it warm.
instructions.3: Sauté the tomatoes in the same oil, season and cook until the sauce thickens.
instructions.4: Lay the toast in a serving dish, spread with the warm tomato sauce and top with the lamb.
instructions.5: Stir the paprika, salt and pepper into the yogurt and pour it over the meat.

ec-430.title: Zucchini with Onion and Mint (Kosa bi-l-Na‘na‘)
ec-430.culturalNotes: Recipe 430, page 186 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Peel the zucchini and slice into rounds about 2 cm thick. Slice the onions very thinly and rub them with salt.
instructions.2: Soften the onions in oil.
instructions.3: Add the zucchini and leave over a very low heat for about 20 minutes, until they have reabsorbed their own juice.
instructions.4: Sprinkle with the mint.

ec-432.title: Zucchini Simmered in Yogurt with Mint (Kosa Matbukha bi-l-Zabadi)
ec-432.culturalNotes: Recipe 432, page 187 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Peel the zucchini and slice into rounds about 2 cm thick.
instructions.2: Cook them over a very low heat until they give up their juice, then drain.
instructions.3: Stir the egg white into the yogurt (it stops the yogurt curdling) and press it through a sieve over the zucchini.
instructions.4: Season and cook uncovered for 15–20 minutes.
